chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not correct for the man that he sell by a Sa'a (a unit of measurement of four handfuls) of other than a Sa'a of the city.

key_terms.صَاعٍ: A unit of volume measurement, typically four handfuls, used for dry goods.
key_terms.صَاعِ الْمِصْرِ: The standard measure of the city/locality, implying the customary local standard.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using non-standard measures in Islamic sales transactions?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia legal principle of adhering to local customary standards ('urf) in commercial transactions to prevent ambiguity and fraud. By mandating the use of the 'Sa' of the city, it emphasizes that contractual validity relies on the specific, recognized measures of the marketplace, a concept central to Usul al-Fiqh discussions on variable legal rulings based on context.
